Hi Emma — great to hear team liked the demo. Short answer: yes, we can support split promo buckets, but there are a few operational caveats.

What we can do today:
- Create two promo allocations linked to the same customer/org id; each allocation gets its own line in the billing export (usage_by_allocation).
- Set labels so you can map them back to Sandbox (60%) and Staging (40%).

Things to confirm from your side:
- Do you want separate consumption thresholds or a combined cap? (E.g., if one bucket exhausts, should it bleed into the other?)
- Do you want distinct expiration dates for each bucket?

I’ll pull in Ben and Lauren to confirm accounting and any pricing/contract implications.

– Logan

Emma — happy to help. Operationally we can create two promo allocations. A couple notes from pricing:

- We treat promotional allowances as contra-revenue (accounting calls it a credit memo applied on top of invoices), so the simplest path for your accounting team is to receive a single invoice with a line showing the promotional credit(s).
- If you want the credits to be represented as separate lines in the monthly invoice, we can do that (we’ll surface allocation IDs in the invoice export).
- No additional charge from Redwood for the split itself; the promo is covered.

One caveat: if you intend to transfer unused promo to a corporate card or reallocate across legal entities, that requires a signed amendment to the MA. Otherwise unused promo simply expires per the promo terms.

I’m attaching the latest pricing sheet and a sample invoice export format so your AP team can see the line-level detail.

Best,

Hi Emma — quick tax/finance note from our side:

- For US entities, Redwood records promotional allowances as contra-revenue (a reduction on the invoice), not as a taxable transfer. Your AP should see the promo lines as invoice credits; tax treatment typically follows how your accounting team treats contra-revenue.
- We can provide a supplemental memo that your tax/accounting team can attach to the invoice showing allocation IDs and expiration dates.
- If BrightLaunch needs the promo to appear as a prepaid asset on your books, that is a different treatment and will require a short amendment (and sign-off) expressing the parties’ intent.

Irene Choi
Accounting Manager
Redwood Inference
